documents.title: Guidance on the Use of Generative AI and Large Language Model Tools
documents.stance_why: The memo says it will "encourage the responsible use" of GenAI and "support a responsible, measured experimentation", but conditions use on disclosure, data protection, output review and the honor code. It sets no tiers and does not hand the decision to instructors, so permit.
documents.summary: Initial Provost and COO guidance (October 2023) for the whole Caltech community on GenAI and LLM tools. It welcomes responsible use and sets four principles: disclosure, data protection, content responsibility and the honor code. It says it is provisional and defers to course instructors and publishers.

units.why: The opening states the purpose: "encourage the responsible use" of GenAI in research, education and administration. This is a default stance welcoming use, so P02 (permit or encourage by default); the conditions come in later units.
units.anchor: encourage the responsible use of generative artificial intelligence

units.why: "Such as OpenAI's ChatGPT and Dall-E and Google's Bard" names which tools the guidance covers, so it sets scope: P61 (definition and scope), informs.
units.anchor: tools and technologies, such as OpenAI's ChatGPT and Dall-E and Google's Bard
units.policy: The guidance covers generative AI and large language model tools and technologies, such as ChatGPT, Dall-E and Bard.

units.why: "We support a responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies" gives the institution's rationale and stance toward AI; this is a principle, closest to P56 (framework) rather than P44, which is about teaching AI as a career skill.
units.anchor: we support a responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies

units.why: "Caltech requires that you follow all existing applicable regulations and Institute policies" binds everyone using GenAI to existing rules rather than creating new ones; it is a framework principle (P56), must.
units.anchor: Caltech requires that you follow all existing applicable regulations and Institute policies

units.why: The list names "ensuring protection of confidential, personal, or business information and intellectual property" as an existing obligation that applies to GenAI use. Intellectual property protection fits P52 best; data privacy itself is coded separately under P50.
units.anchor: ensuring protection of confidential, personal, or business information and intellectual property
units.frag_start: These include, but are not limited to,

units.why: The guidance says it is "written for the present moment and will likely evolve alongside the technology", a statement that the policy is provisional, so P54.
units.anchor: will likely evolve alongside the technology
units.frag_start: Likewise, our guidance for the appropriate

units.why: "Always disclose promptly, or reference the use of GenAI tools" is a direct requirement on users to disclose AI use, so P24, must.
units.anchor: always disclose promptly, or reference the use of GenAI tools and application plug-ins

units.why: The sentence says disclosure "reduces misunderstandings regarding the source of information, potentially limiting claims of academic dishonesty or plagiarism". It describes how disclosure affects integrity claims, so P28 (not P24, which is the requirement itself), informs.
units.anchor: potentially limiting claims of academic dishonesty or plagiarism
units.policy: Disclosure reduces misunderstandings about the source of information, potentially limiting claims of academic dishonesty or plagiarism.

units.why: "Follow the guidance provided by the course instructor" hands the specific rule on AI use in writing to the instructor, so P04 (instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: follow the guidance provided by the course instructor
units.frag_start: When using GenAI to write or
units.policy: When using GenAI to write or publish, follow the guidance provided by the course instructor.

units.why: The example that publishers "may require that the GenAI be included as an author" concerns publication venues, so it is P62 (research and scholarship, deferring to venue rules).
units.anchor: some may require that the GenAI be included as an author
units.policy: Journal or manuscript publishers differ: some may require that GenAI be included as an author, others only acknowledgement.

units.why: "Uploading content into GenAI (Open GenAI) is a public disclosure" is a factual warning about data exposure; it is privacy information (P50), informs.
units.anchor: uploading content into GenAI (Open GenAI) is a public disclosure
units.frag_start: Unless you are using a GenAI

units.why: "Do not enter, contribute, or otherwise input sensitive, confidential, or restricted information into Open GenAI tools" prohibits a specific data use, so P50 (protect personal data), must-not.
units.anchor: input sensitive, confidential, or restricted information into Open GenAI tools

units.why: "Caltech is considering a subscription to a restricted GenAI" says the institution may provide a sanctioned tool, so P17, informs; it is not yet an offered tool.
units.anchor: Caltech is considering a subscription to a restricted GenAI

units.why: Caltech "reserve[s] the right to disable or limit access to AI companion tools in enterprise business software" such as Zoom and Office, which concerns AI embedded in software; P07 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: disable or limit access to AI companion tools in enterprise business software
units.policy: Caltech reserves the right to disable or limit access to AI companion tools in enterprise business software and applications, such as Zoom and Microsoft Office suites.

units.why: "You should always review and assess all output generated by GenAI tools for accuracy" tells users to verify AI output because "GenAI systems are fallible", so P31, should.
units.anchor: you should always review and assess all output generated by GenAI tools for accuracy

units.why: The honor code quote "No member of the Caltech community shall take unfair advantage" is said to extend to GenAI, applying existing integrity rules to AI misuse; nearest type P36, though no sanction is stated.
units.anchor: No member of the Caltech community shall take unfair advantage of any other member
units.frag_start: Caltech's honor code underscores the importance
units.policy: Caltech's honor code extends to the use of GenAI tools: no member of the Caltech community shall take unfair advantage of any other member.

units.why: The guidance points to "teaching resources that have already been provided by the Center for Teaching, Learning, and Outreach", which is support for instructors, so P63.
units.anchor: teaching resources that have already been provided by the
units.frag_end: Center for Teaching, Learning, and Outreach
units.policy: The guidelines are offered in addition to teaching resources provided by the Center for Teaching, Learning, and Outreach.

units.why: The closing says the guidance "fosters a community that values transparency, integrity, privacy, accuracy, and fairness", a statement of principles, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: fosters a community that values transparency, integrity, privacy, accuracy, and fairness

units.why: "Caltech may update its guidance as the technology and regulatory and commercial landscapes evolve" states a revision possibility distinct from the earlier note; P54, informs.
units.anchor: Caltech may update its guidance as the technology and regulatory and commercial landscapes evolve

notes: Single university-layer document; no student-facing course rules. Cloudflare blocks caltech.edu, so the studentaffairs copy was coded.
